BiblicalUsage: Zaraq is sprinkling, the tossing of blood or water onto something to mark it as God's. Moses sprinkles the blood of the covenant on the people at Sinai, the priests sprinkle the blood of the offering around the altar, and Ezekiel promises a day when God Himself will sprinkle clean water on His people and make them clean. The same word also warns that anyone who touches a dead body and refuses the sprinkled water of cleansing remains unclean.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sprinkling teaches us that cleansing comes from outside ourselves, applied by God and not achieved by us. No one sprinkles himself clean; the blood and the water must be brought to us. My position is that all this sprinkling points to Christ, whose blood was shed once and still speaks, and whose cleansing reaches deeper than any water could.
